blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — A bill that seeks to empower the government with the legal framework to counter transnational drug syndicates involved in narco-terrorism has been filed in the House of Representatives. In a statement on Tuesday, Las Piñas Rep. Mark Anthony Santos, chairperson of the House committee on dangerous drugs, said that he has filed House Bill (HB) No. 11751 or the proposed Anti-Narco-Terrorism Act of 2026, which will qualify transnational drug-trafficking organizations as terrorist organizations. Santos said the bill will amend both the Anti-Terrorism Act of 2020 and the Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002 to address potential jurisdictional gaps […]...
